newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks surge on higher foreign stakes.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks surge on higher foreign stakes.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks continued marching ahead on Thursday with brokers saying an increase in the level of permitted foreign shareholdings had given the market's current bull-run further impetus.
The key industrial index jumped 76.04 points -- or 1.2 percent -- to close at 6,241, a new all time high.
"The market is looking very upbeat. There's a lot of good news around, including yesterday's announcement on foreign investment, so that has added to the bull-run," one broker said.
On Wednesday, the Reserve Bank raised to 40 percent from 35 percent the amount of shareholding foreigners are allowed to buy in a Zimbabwean company.

In measures Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE) officials and market analysts said would stimulate fresh flows of foreign investment, the bank also said a single investor could now own up to 10 percent of the equity of a listed company, compared to five percent previously.
On the ZSE on Thursday, bankers FMB led the day's winners, surging 150 cents to 3,350, followed by timber producer Border 100 cents higher at 1,300 and food group Cairns 65 cents up at 690.

Finance group Finhold jumped 60 cents to 700, Truworths rose 30 cents to 700, multi-industrial group Tedco at 400, sugar producer Hippo at 750 and Alloys at 850 all gained 25 cents while Natfoods climbed 20 cents to 600, refrigerator-maker Capri added 15 cents to 110 and TA Holdings put on 17 cents to 147.
Soft drinks manufacturer Schweppes was the day's sole loser, shedding 10 cents to 610.
Minings were quieter with Falgold unchanged at 175 while Wankie Colliery rose 10 cents to 340. The mining index edged a slight 1.17 points up to end at 1,320.77.
